claims.text: The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.

Pulumi emits placeholder text of the form `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` when an Output is converted to a string (e.g., in logs, generated files, or resource properties) instead of yielding its value.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value causes errors.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" for update conflicts.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon can cause crashes or hangs.
The CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (instead of via apply) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message.
In TypeScript, the string conversion of an Output contains literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling JSON.stringify() on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to json.dumps() fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; Output.json_dumps() should be used instead.
In Go, passing a pulumi.StringOutput where a string is expected is a compile error.
In C#, string conversion of an Output contains literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true (for TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

String-composition helpers: pulumi.interpolate and pulumi.concat in TypeScript, Output.concat/Output.format/Output.json_dumps in Python, pulumi.Sprintf/pulumi.JSONMarshal in Go, and Output.Format in C#.
The apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished; the callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a few positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In dynamically typed languages an `if` on an Output is generally always true because the Output object is evaluated; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error.
Values known at program start, such as pulumi.Config stack configuration, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Using an Output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, range(some_output) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.
Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously read a resolved value from an Output; awaiting or reading it either fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
Linked pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs.
